board: AG32VF303CCT6 / L48, SRAM configuration through a single controlled board client

afexe_absent_board_20260929.definition: Pips isolated on the board by single-net bisection plus one-pip avoidance of a stable wrong default image, each unknown to the vendor bitgen: RMUX57@16,3->RMUX34@16,4 (minmax32_kat, lfsr16x7_kat, stronger fast-RAM holdout; codeword [2,9] belongs to RMUX09 four rows below, absent in row 4); RMUX14@14,1->RMUX61@14,2 (stronger fast-RAM holdout seed 3; the vendor bitgen aborts the tile, and [2,9] in row 2 selects no vendor source); RMUX03@14,6->RMUX15@14,6 (stronger slow-RAM holdout seed 3; absent in four vendor-bitgen contexts although 26 board-passing images used it).
afexe_absent_board_20260929.policy: Post-route refusal plus the existing retry penalty. The device graph and profile identities are unchanged.

afexe_absent_20260929.definition: Every other shipped fabric ROUTE pip with a routing-multiplexer destination in rows 1-12 whose vendor-bitgen probes include absent or burst and never same, unless a shipped silicon-qualified routed fixture uses it. Use by board-passing images does not exempt a pip: RMUX03@14,6->RMUX15@14,6 was used by 26 of them and still caused a stable wrong image.
afexe_absent_20260929.policy: Post-route refusal plus the existing retry penalty. Admit a pip only with a design-level silicon test that depends on it.

afexe_codeword_conflict_20260930.definition: RMUX08@2,4->RMUX33@1,4 (its codeword is the vendor's codeword for RMUX56@5,4) and five IO-row hops without a pad-feed row whose emitted bytes differ from the bytes the vendor bitgen writes. The vendor-bitgen oracle is not calibrated in the IO rows (y=0, y=13), so IO-row hops are refused only on a byte mismatch; pad-feed hops whose bytes match are kept.
afexe_codeword_conflict_20260930.policy: Post-route refusal plus the existing retry penalty.

method: Same placement and LUT connections throughout. The failing and passing minmax32_kat routed checkpoints re-encode byte-identically to their board images. Hybrid routings (subsets of nets rerouted with every other net held) were encoded by this repository's bitgen, which validated each one, and loaded into SRAM between reference images.

observations.result: The failing routing fails at 4, 10 and 40 MHz; the passing routing passes at all three. Not setup timing.
120-net tangle -> one eighth -> net state[4] -> pip RMUX57@16,3->RMUX34@16,4. Only removing that pip passes (2/2); changing its feed while keeping it fails.

Vacating the neighbouring outputs of CFG_RMUX5, vacating RMUX57 at X16Y4 or X16Y8, or also driving RMUX57 at X16Y4 with the same net: all still fail. Driving RMUX57@16,3 through a dead-end stub without the pip passes 3/3.

limitations: One load and one reset release per board observation.
The 40 oracle rows are refused on vendor-topology evidence alone. Oracle-absent pips that a shipped silicon-qualified fixture uses stay admitted. A false-positive refusal costs one unused pip.
Ring-oscillator witnesses do not certify a pip for design use: the board-proven pip has one.
oracle_sweep_2026_09_30: Of 1,596 shipped pips the 09-19 oracle marked 'different', none is emitted with a wrong codeword: 1,430 lacked a table row (the flow emits af.exe's codeword), 108 had a stale table cfg string the emitter does not use, 59 were base-route overlaps, and 8 BRAM X13Y4 inputs emit af.exe's bytes from bram_pip_cfg.csv. Of 136 shipped codeword-collision groups, only the two rows above are real conflicts. Oracle 'absent' verdicts in the IO rows (y=0, y=13) are artefacts of tile labelling; the six IO-row pips already refused stay refused because their emitted bytes differ from af.exe's.
